narrative.overview:
Teikio is used tableside, mid-service, often one-handed, by someone who can't afford to fumble the screen. The system reads like paper and ink: a white (or cream, or charcoal) page, gray paper surfaces, and ink-black as the one voice that marks what you can press. Controls are drawn the way you'd rule a notebook: tight 6px corners, a 1px ink line around anything outlined, and a single medium-weight sans carrying every size from page titles down to status pills. Nothing decorative competes with the task. There are no gradients, no display face and no ornamental icons, because the interface's job is to disappear into the order, the table or the ticket in front of the user.

The Material-shaped color roles (`primary` / `onPrimary` / `primaryContainer` / `secondary` / `secondaryContainer` / `surface*` / `onSurfaceVariant` / `inverseSurface`) already speak Android's language, even though the components are hand-built rather than native Material widgets. That middle ground is deliberate, and the system should keep leaning into it as it moves toward fuller Android conformance rather than abandon it for something more decorative.
keyCharacteristics: One typeface (Plus Jakarta Sans), one accent (ink), no display/body pairing.
Core primitives (cards, buttons, chips, inputs, selects, grouped rows) share a tight 6px radius. Larger radii are kept for touch-only controls and floating chrome.
Outlines are drawn in ink (`primary`) on interactive elements. The pale hairline (`border`) is for resting fields and quiet dividers.
Thin-stroke Lucide icons throughout, from one family, tinted `icon` gray by default.
Two-tier elevation: content sits flat, and only floating elements cast a shadow.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Ink is the only brand color. Selection is the Ink-Blue Wash, not a tint of the primary, and status is the semantic four, never the primary. Accent-like UI (spinners, checkmarks, focus borders) uses `primary`, never a hard-coded `blue-500`, and blue appears only where it means *info*. If a screen seems to need a second brand color, that's a decision for `new-work`, not a local choice.

rules.name: The Roles, Not Colors Rule
rules.body: Every color comes from a role in `constants/theme.ts` (`Palette`), used as a prefix-free class (`bg-surface`, `text-on-surface-variant`, `border-primary`) or through `usePalette()` / `tw.color()` when a prop needs a raw value. Never hard-code a hex, `white` or `bg-white` on a themed surface, and never compute a color in a module-level `StyleSheet.create`, because it won't follow the theme.

rules.name: The Medium-Body Rule
rules.body: Default body text is medium (500). Only `body2` drops to regular. Don't default new body copy to regular weight, because it will read lighter than everything around it.

rules.name: The Bold-Status Rule
rules.body: Status `Label` text is bold (700), or semibold on the `outline` color. A pill is read at a glance across a busy screen, so its text carries more weight than the body text next to it.

rules.name: The Flat-Content Rule
rules.body: Content surfaces (cards, list rows, inputs, chips) don't cast shadows. The only resting shadow is the explicit `elevated` card. Shadows are for things that float: docked chrome gets `shadow-sm`, free-floating elements get `shadow-lg`, and there are no other weights.

rules.name: The 6px Rule
rules.body: Any new content primitive, whether a card, button, chip, input or list tile, takes the 6px radius. Use 24px only for a touch-only control or its track, 16px only for a free-floating element, and the pill only for status, the floating toolbar or a circular control. Never round a content container fully.

rules.name: The Ink-Line Rule
rules.body: An outlined *interactive* element (outline button, outline card, unselected chip, checkbox) is drawn with a 1px ink line (`border-primary`). The pale hairline (`border`) is reserved for resting text fields, the outlined icon button, the outline label and dividers, all elements that should recede until touched.

rules.name: The Always-Enabled Rule
rules.body: A blockable action (replacing an item that's already been delivered, editing a variant once some of it has shipped) stays visually enabled and tappable. The specific reason it can't proceed surfaces inline the moment its sheet or card opens. It's never shown as a grayed-out state and never explained by an `Alert` fired on tap. When two blocks always fire together, show the reason once. Once units are delivered, the variant choices in the order-detail sheet are hidden rather than dimmed, and the Replace section's reason is the only explanation shown.

dos: **Do** give every new card, button, chip, input or list tile the 6px radius (`rounded-md`).
**Do** draw outlined interactive elements with a 1px ink line (`border-primary`), and keep the pale `border` hairline for resting fields and dividers.
**Do** use the Ink-Blue Wash (`secondary`) for selected/active state, never a tint of the primary.
**Do** default new text fields and selects to `outlined`.
**Do** pick a status `Label` by `color` alone. It's one solid pastel style with bold text.
**Do** render an inactive record as its card at 50% opacity.
**Do** put "more options" behind an `ActionsBottomSheet` in Edit → Activate/Deactivate → Delete order, with delete in red.
**Do** keep a blockable action enabled and show its specific reason inline when the sheet or card opens.
**Do** use Lucide icons through the shared `Icon` component, sized 16–24px (up to 32px+ only in vertical buttons), and let it fall back to the `icon` role color.
**Do** keep body text at medium weight (500), and drop to regular only for `body2`.
donts: **Don't** introduce a second accent color. Ink is the only brand hue, and status uses the fixed semantic four.
**Don't** put a shadow on a resting content surface other than `Card variant="elevated"`, or invent a shadow weight beyond `shadow-sm` (docked) and `shadow-lg` (free-floating).
**Don't** copy the 8–24px radii still found in older screen-level views onto new content. They're migration debt.
**Don't** reintroduce a soft/tinted `Label` style or a status dot on labels.
**Don't** reach for a full-screen `Modal` beyond a short yes/no confirmation. Options and pickers go in a bottom sheet.
**Don't** hard-code colors (`#fff`, `"#999"`, `bg-white`, `text-white` on a surface). Use a role so Paper and Dark keep working.
**Don't** mix icon families. It's Lucide only, with no Ionicons, Material icons or filled sets.
